task_instruction:
Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hi there! I'm having trouble with my mobile data — it either stops working completely or is just really slow. I'd really like to get it sorted out and get a fast, reliable connection on my phone. I don't have access to Wi-Fi right now, so mobile data is all I've got.

turns.thought:
I'd be happy to help you troubleshoot your mobile data. To get started, I'll need to locate your account.

Could you please provide your **phone number** (or your **full name and date of birth**)?
turns.execution_output: User: Sure! My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002.

turns.thought:
I found your account. Here's what I see for your line **555-123-2002**:

- **Status:** Active
- **Plan:** Premium Plan (15.0 GB monthly data limit)
- **Data used this cycle:** 15.1 GB — you've **exceeded your 15.0 GB limit**
- **Billing cycle ends:** 2025-02-28

That's very likely why your data has stopped working or slowed down — once a line goes past its plan's data limit, data connectivity is affected.

To restore your connection, you have two options:
1. **Refuel data** — add extra data to this line at your plan's rate of **$2.00 per GB** (maximum 2 GB = up to $4.00). This would be added to your current bill.
2. **Change to a plan with more data** — note your last plan change was 2025-01-10/2024-12-15, so I'd need to review available options with you.

How much data would you like to refuel (up to 2 GB)? If you'd like, I can add the full 2 GB for **$4.00** right now.
turns.execution_output: User: Ah, that makes sense — I had no idea I'd gone over my limit. I definitely don't want to change my plan, but I'm happy to add the extra data. Yes, please go ahead and add the full 2 GB for $4.00.

turns.thought: I'll go ahead and add the 2 GB refuel to your line.
turns.execution_output: {"message": "Successfully added 2 GB of data for line L1002 for $4.00", "new_data_refueling_gb": "2.0", "charge": "4.0"}

turns.thought:
Done! I've added **2 GB** of data to line **555-123-2002**.

**Confirmation:**
- Data added: 2.0 GB
- Charge: **$4.00** (at your Premium Plan rate of $2.00/GB), applied to your current bill
- Your available data for the rest of this billing cycle: 2.0 GB (cycle ends **2025-02-28**)

**Next step:** Please reboot your device so the additional data takes effect and your connection is restored.

One thing to keep in mind: your usage (15.1 GB) is right at the edge of your 15.0 GB plan limit, and refueling is capped at 2 GB per cycle. Once your cycle resets on **2025-02-28**, your full 15.0 GB allowance will be available again.

Is your data working now after rebooting? If it's still slow or not connecting, let me know and I'll help you look into it further.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me restart my phone now.

turns.thought:
Thanks — that's very helpful. There are a few things on your status bar that could each be dragging your speed down. Let's work through them one at a time.

**1. Network type is stuck on 2G** — this is the biggest one. 2G is very slow and isn't really suitable for data use. On your phone, please go to **Settings → Network / Mobile Networks → Preferred network mode** and set it to **4G/5G preferred** (instead of 2G).

Once you've changed that, tell me what network type shows in your status bar and I'll take you to the next step.

While you're there, you can also **turn Data Saver OFF** — it restricts background data and can make apps and browsing feel slow or unresponsive even when data is working. I'll confirm the remaining VPN item after we see whether the network change helps.
turns.execution_output: User: I can only make one change at a time, so let me start with the network mode.

turns.thought:
Yes — let's do Data Saver next.

On your phone, please go to **Settings → Network & Internet → Data Saver** and turn it **OFF**. Data Saver restricts background data usage, which can make apps and browsing feel slow or unresponsive even when your connection is fine.

One thing to flag: with Data Saver off, your apps will use data more freely. You currently have **2.0 GB** available for the rest of this cycle (through **2025-02-28**).

Once that's off, let me know:
1. Whether browsing and apps now load normally
2. Whether the **VPN** is one you intentionally use — I'd like to take a look at that next, since an active VPN can significantly reduce data speeds

We'll deal with the VPN only if your speed is still not where you want it.

That's a very important detail — thanks for mentioning France. Since you're outside your home network, your line needs to be **roaming enabled** to use mobile data abroad. Let me check and fix that on our side right away.

Thanks — that's an important detail! Since you're **abroad in France**, you're outside your home network, so roaming is involved. Good news: I've just **enabled roaming on your line (555-123-2002) at no cost** — I've verified it's now active.

Now two things to do:

**1. Turn ON Data Roaming on the phone (important!)**
Even though roaming is enabled on your line, your phone has its own separate switch. Please go to **Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile Network → Roaming** and turn **Data Roaming ON**. Without this, your phone won't connect to data networks while you're abroad.

**2. Check the VPN**
Since you don't remember setting one up, let's look at it. Go to **Settings → Network & Internet → VPN** and tell me:
- Is it actually connected (connected vs. just saved/on)?
- What's the **performance/speed level** shown?

If the VPN shows **"ON and connected" with performance "Poor"**, I'd recommend disconnecting it — go ahead and **disconnect the VPN**. An active VPN routes your traffic through an extra server and can slow things down considerably, especially while roaming.

Once you've turned on Data Roaming and dealt with the VPN, please **run a speed test** and let me know the result. That'll tell us whether your connection is where it should be on 5G.

(Also worth noting: while roaming, data use can add up quickly — you have **2.0 GB** available through **2025-02-28**.)
turns.execution_output: User: I'll take these one at a time. Let me start with turning on Data Roaming.

turns.thought:
You're very welcome — glad we got you up and running on an Excellent 275 Mbps connection!

Yes, your understanding is correct. Here's a quick recap of where things stand:

**Your line (555-123-2002)**
- Plan: **Premium Plan** (unchanged — 15.0 GB/month, $65.00/month)
- Refueled data: **2.0 GB** remaining, valid through the end of your billing cycle on **2025-02-28**
- Charge for the refuel: **$4.00** (added to your current bill)
- Roaming: **enabled on your line** (at no cost)
- Line status: **Active**

**Settings to keep as they are while you're in France**
- Network mode: **4G/5G preferred** (you're on 5G now — leaving it on 2G/3G was the original cause of the slowdown)
- **Data Saver: OFF**
- **Data Roaming: ON** — this is essential while you're outside your home network
- **VPN: disconnected** — if it reconnects on its own and speeds drop, disconnect it again

**Two things worth watching:**
1. **Your data balance** — you have 2.0 GB left this cycle, and roaming can use data quickly. If it runs out, data connectivity will be affected again, and refueling is capped at 2 GB. Your full 15.0 GB allowance resets on **2025-02-28**.
2. **Your usage is right at your plan's limit** (15.1 GB used vs. 15.0 GB included), so you may hit the same wall again next cycle. Refueling is always available, and changing to a plan with more data is an option if you'd rather not manage it month to month — no pressure, just so you know.

Also, since you mentioned you don't recall setting up the VPN, it may be worth reviewing that app's settings on your device at some point so it doesn't reconnect unexpectedly.

Anything else I can help you with today?
turns.execution_output:
User: That all makes sense, thank you for the clear summary. I'll keep an eye on my data balance while I'm here and make sure those settings stay as they are. I'm happy with the Excellent speed now, so I think we're all set.

Thanks again for your help — have a great day!
